commands.does: set a key's value

tinystore kv ./data set counts hits 42 --as int
echo '{"theme": "dark"}' | tinystore kv ./data set settings 42 - --as json

flags.means: a bucket the program opened from this database, kept in sql/<db>.db

commands.more: A value is text unless --as says otherwise, and nothing is guessed from how it looks, so 02134 stays text. - reads the value from stdin, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops the quotes inside a JSON argument. Sending the same set again changes nothing. It writes through the server that holds the directory, or starts one that stops 30 s after its last client; a directory a program holds inside its own process is refused.
commands.name: kv set

commands.does: change a config's live settings, which its programs take at once

Only a live setting changes, checked against its rules, as the store keeps it. It goes through the server that holds the directory, or one it starts, so that every program holding the config takes the change at once.

commands.does: write the Prometheus text on stdin to the store's metrics
examples: curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | tinystore metrics ./data ingest --label instance=web-1
ping … | awk '…' | tinystore metrics ./data ingest -f --kind ping_lost_total=counter

flags.means: follow a stream that does not end, written every second; a line it cannot read is skipped
flags.name: -f

flags.means: a name's type where the stream gives no # TYPE, as x_total=counter; with -f
flags.name: --kind

flags.means: a label every series of the text gets; again for more
flags.name: --label

flags.means: how long each name of the text keeps its samples, as 30d; 30d when never given
flags.name: --keep

commands.more: Every series of the text is written, or none, in Prometheus' format or OpenMetrics'. With -f, Prometheus' text alone is read a line at a time and written every second or 10,000 lines; a line it cannot read, or the store refuses, is said and skipped, and the command ends 1. A name with no type is a gauge. It writes through the server that holds the directory, or starts one that stops 30 s after its last client; a directory a program holds inside its own process is refused. A sample given no time takes the time it was read, the same when a lost write is sent again.
commands.name: metrics ingest

commands.does: let an AI agent read the store, and write what --write names
examples: claude mcp add tinystore -- tinystore mcp ./data
claude mcp add tinystore -- tinystore mcp ./data --write kv_set,jobs_add

flags.means: the tools that write it offers, as kv_set,jobs_add, or all; none when absent
flags.name: --write

commands.more: The Model Context Protocol on stdin and stdout. Its tools that read: status, logs, kv_get, kv_list, jobs_list, sql_query and search_list. Those that write, a tool an operation, only as --write names them: kv_set, kv_delete, jobs_add, jobs_cancel, files_put, files_delete, events_append, channels_publish, config_update, config_reset and sql_exec. Each is marked as writing, and as destructive where it removes or replaces something, so that the agent's host asks for each; they write through the server that holds the directory, or one they start.
commands.name: mcp

commands.does: a token line for serve's --tokens
commands.more: admin may do anything, data reads and writes the store, read only reads it.
commands.name: token

commands.does: run a command while it holds a key of a lock

flags.means: stand in line this long for the key, 10s when not given; 0 takes it only if free
flags.name: --wait

flags.means: how long the lease lasts from each renewal, 30s when not given
flags.name: --ttl

flags.means: let the key go this long after it was given, however it is renewed
flags.name: --max-hold

commands.more: The key is held through the server that holds the directory, or one it starts, and its lease renewed every third of --ttl while the command runs. The command gets the lease's fence in TINYSTORE_FENCE, is stopped if the lease is lost, and the key is let go once it ends; the command's exit is this one's. A key held by another past --wait exits 1 and runs nothing.
commands.name: lock hold

words.<command>: the command to run, with its own arguments
words.<config>: a config's name, as its program opened it
words.<db>: one of the application's databases, kept in sql/<db>.db
words.<host>: a host name or an address
words.<json>: JSON: an object, a list, a string or a number; - reads it from stdin
words.<migrations>: a directory of migration files, 0001_users.sql and on
words.<name>: the name of what the command reads or changes: a metric, or an index
words.<op>: what an aggregate computes: count, sum, avg, min, max, increase, rate, or p and a rank, as p95
words.<path=value>: a live setting's path and its value, as model.max_tokens=2048; path:=json for JSON
words.<path>: a file's path in its set
words.<value>: the value: text unless --as says int or json; - reads it from stdin
words.[admin|data|read]: what a token lets its client do: everything, data alone, or read
words.[branch]: the keys under a branch, its owners as 42/devices
words.[db]: one of the application's databases; every one when left out
words.[dir]: the store's directory; the current one when left out
words.[field=text|field:=json]: what an event carries: field=text for text, field:=json for JSON
words.[file]: one file of the store, as sql/app.db; every one when left out
words.[name]: the event's name; without one, each line of stdin is an event
words.[path]: a setting or a group; every change when left out
words.[prefix]: only the names, ids or paths that start with it
